title: Right-angle-free sets in the honeycomb grid
statement: Let the honeycomb grid H_N be the points (a, b) of the triangular grid T_N (the points a + b w, w = e^(i pi/3), a, b >= 0, a + b <= N - 1) with a - b not divisible by 3. Removing the index-3 sublattice of hexagon centres from the triangular lattice leaves the honeycomb lattice of graphene, with unit bonds; the squared distance is da^2 + da db + db^2. Determine the largest number of points of the honeycomb grid H_N such that no three of them form a right angle (no three points p, q, r with (q - p).(r - p) = 0), as a function of N. The exact values are known (ours) for N <= 12; the headline cell is N = 15: find 22 or more such points of the region of side 15.
submission: Text file: one point 'a b' per line, a point of the region of side 15 (lines starting with # are ignored).
score: the number of points (larger is better)

best_known.source: Quantavane (Arhan Canli), 10 November 2026: 21 points of the region of side 15 with no right angle (no three points p, q, r with (q - p).(r - p) = 0), the best set CP-SAT found in 10 seconds, started from the set for side N - 1 (tools/lattice_sets.py)

context: A set of points is right-angle-free when no three of its points form a right angle. Gamble, Pulleyblank, Reed and Shepherd (1995) studied the largest right-angle-free subsets of the plane and of the square lattice, and related work (Junger and Pulleyblank) shows the problem NP-hard for general point sets; sets without isosceles right triangles in the n x n grid are a separate, active question (OEIS A271906; arXiv:2607.22828, 2026). The honeycomb lattice (the carbon sites of graphene) is the triangular lattice with a third of its points removed, so fewer right angles are available. The exact values grow irregularly, with no closed form in sight; how fast they grow is open.
references: B. Gamble, W. Pulleyblank, B. Reed, B. Shepherd, Right angle free subsets in the plane, Graphs and Combinatorics 11 (1995) 121-129
A Salem-Spencer-type construction for large subsets of integer grids with no isosceles right triangles, arXiv:2607.22828 (2026)
OEIS A271906 (largest subsets of the n x n grid with no right isosceles triangle)

novelty.verdict: new question for this lattice: right-angle-free subsets are studied for the square lattice (Gamble, Pulleyblank, Reed and Shepherd 1995; Junger and Pulleyblank) and isosceles right triangles in the square grid (A271906); no result was found for the honeycomb grid, and its first values are not in the OEIS.
closest: B. Gamble, W. Pulleyblank, B. Reed and B. Shepherd (1995): right-angle-free subsets of the plane and of the square lattice; another lattice.
OEIS A271906 and arXiv:2607.22828: no isosceles right triangle in the square grid, a weaker condition in another lattice.

baseline.text: 21 for N = 15, held by Quantavane (Arhan Canli), 10 November 2026: the points in `refs/hex-right.txt` (the best set CP-SAT found in 10 seconds, started from the set for side N - 1 (tools/lattice_sets.py)). Exact values for N = 2..12: 2, 3, 3, 6, 8, 8, 10, 11, 11, 14, 16 (CP-SAT (OR-Tools 9.15, one worker) proved the optimum of the 0/1 model in tools/lattice_sets.py).
